posts.name: Sonvar
posts.cooked:
As Christopher commented to someone else in the update the box is not the cause of the delays 

>

Christopher Badell Collaborator 1 day ago

I am sorry to hear that there are some of you who are not excited about the Ultimate Collector's Case. That said, the overwhelming response has been positive, so we're still upbeat about it. 

For those of you who believe that the case is the only reason for the delay, worry not! It's not just the case! It's also that designing eleven heroes, five environments, and an entirely new mode for such a big game takes time. Totally on me, design-wise. Not the case's fault. I'll talk more about the design and its ups and downs next Tuesday.

And for folks who have ordered the case but are now sad that it's not everything they'd hoped, wait until you have it in hand to decide. At that point, if you're still disappointed, there will probably be a healthy after-market for it, as we're certainly going to have to sell it for a higher MSRP than we offered it for on the Kickstarter. It's hefty!

Don't worry, everyone. The end of the Multiverse is still on its way.

posts.cooked:
I don't know.  It seems like the box design is overly complex.  I can fit the entire hero, villains, and environment decks in Smash Up's Big Geeky Box with a bit of room to spare.  It probably won't fit OblivAeon.  That said, add a couple of inches to the depth and add some space to the top and you could fit a shelf that would hold the instructions, tokens, and oversized villain cards.  Build it like a standard board game box and you've got an eligent, simple design.

During the Kickstarter I was excited at the initial concept art of the collector’s box, but when I saw the samples in update 33 I lost a lot of that enthusiasm.  I hope they can come up with a good design that doesn’t look overly complex and holds up over time.  Guess we’ll have to wait till July.

Of course the big question is if it be big enough to fit the new Sentinels of Earth-Prime.

Ben

posts.name: Medic-Tank
posts.cooked:
I had to step away from playtesting a few months because of real life. Had the pleasure to see that some of the issues that had me railing for the longest time were finally addressed. Playtesting also shifted in gears and is going very fast at the moment. Taking a step back also means realising that the scope of this expansion is bigger than the original core set.

 

Comparable number of heroes 11 instead of 10, but their interaction need to be checked not only amongst themselves but against all previous deck with an attention to the risk of power creeping. To complicate things more these decks had to be tuned to two character cards at once as some ofthose were rushed and imbalanced in vacuum and finalised before the deck.

Greater number of environments than core set 5 against 4.

A whole new villain mode that needs to be epic AND accessible. There is only one try at this as no expansions will patch it's holes. This is the scariest one and has come a very long way. Truth is it probably wont be universaly acclaimed, but it is fun and epic and still takes too much setup and play time.

You're definitely not the only one that feels that way.  OblivAeon will be a little better for me--my game group won't play Vengeance because they hate being responsible for more than their own hero, and I can control OblivAeon all by myself--but smaller, faster game modes are a bigger draw for me.  Even with the app, it takes me maybe an hour and a half to get through one Vengeance game; I can get through two or three normal games in the same amount of time.

I'm actually just as interested in SoEP for exactly this reason, since it adds 4 new villains and environments as well as 10 new heroes.  I'm definitely buying it; the only reason I'm only backing that for $1 is the shipping cost.

Honestly I played Vengence maybe once or twice when it came out and never did again. Couldn't convince my game group to give it more goes and it was more hassle than fun.

I will say that after VotM released that the Vengence format became so much smoother since, in my opinion, the decks were better designed and the influx of different difficulty setups really added to our ability to set up fun games that were not a quagmire to slog through. We still don't play the format all that offten, but we certainly break it out from time to time which is far more than we used to.

OblivAeon will be vastly different than the Vengence format. You can see that just from the Kickstarter hints and previews. It's going through a lot of iterations right now, but the main goal is to create an epic-ness that you won't be able to find in the Standard or Vengence format. If >G nails that feeling, I'll bet dollars to doll hairs that it'll find your table top more than 4 times.
